# Godotwright

> Godotwright is an MCP server, CLI and Claude Code plugin that makes coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, and any agent that speaks MCP or can run a shell command) better at Godot 4.7. It gives them the real Godot 4.7 API offline, a map of the project, headless Godot checks, an AAA review of GDScript, and tools to build, view and check 3D models (.glb) from code. MIT licensed, runs with `npx -y godotwright`.

Install and connect: `npx -y godotwright mcp --tier cheap` (short output, strict steps, for small models) or `--tier premium` (full detail). It is also listed in the official MCP Registry as io.github.laaielichter/godotwright. One-step installs: Claude Code plugin `/plugin install godotwright --marketplace laaielichter/Godotwright` (adds hooks that review every Godot file the agent edits, skills for the Godot workflow, debugging, performance, vehicles, large worlds, 3D models and patches to shipped games, /godotwright:review, /godotwright:port, /godotwright:learn and /godotwright:dream, and eight subagents: godot-reviewer, godot-debugger, godot-migrator, godot-performance, godot-shader-specialist, godot-model-builder, godot-test-engineer and godot-dreamer), Claude Desktop bundle `godotwright.mcpb` from the latest GitHub release, Gemini CLI `gemini extensions install https://github.com/laaielichter/Godotwright`, and one-click links for Cursor and VS Code on the [install page](https://laaielichter.github.io/Godotwright/install.html).

- [Godot workflow skill](https://github.com/laaielichter/Godotwright/blob/main/plugins/godotwright/skills/godot/SKILL.md): how an agent should work in a Godot project with Godotwright

- [Small, cheap models and everyday tasks](https://github.com/laaielichter/Godotwright/blob/main/docs/cheap-models-code.md): twelve small-model agents on six Godot tasks, graded with real Godot, and the five tool fixes that came out of it
- [Benchmark](https://github.com/laaielichter/Godotwright/blob/main/bench/RESULTS.md): 168 agent runs with and without the tools, with the limits stated

- [Privacy](https://github.com/laaielichter/Godotwright/blob/main/PRIVACY.md): nothing leaves the machine unless you opt in; no code, file names or paths are ever sent

## Start here when something is broken

`godotwright doctor [path] [--symptom "what you see"]` (godot_doctor): the review and, when Godot is installed, a headless load of every script and scene, grouped by cause and sorted most urgent first; each problem with its place, the lesson that explains it, the fix, and whether `godotwright fix` (godot_fix) or `godotwright migrate` can do it; then numbered next steps.
`godotwright fix [path] [--write] [--check]` (godot_fix): mechanical fixes for review findings, each labelled safe (only removes the problem) or check (changes more); shows them first, then reviews the changed files again.

## A game session that stays up

`godotwright session start [path] [--scene res://x.tscn]` (godot_session op start): loads the scene once, headless and paused at frame 0, and keeps it running between commands (it quits after 15 idle minutes; `session stop` ends it). `godotwright game tree|get|set|call|eval|step|signals|layout|ray|ui|reload|errors` (godot_game): the live node tree, values read and set, methods called, Godot Expressions evaluated, `layout` (where 3D objects are and whether they rest on, float above or sink into what is below), `ray` (what a physics ray hits), `ui --size 1280x720 --size 720x1280` (clipped labels, off-screen panels, overlapping buttons), and `step <frames> --input "..." --watch Node.prop --until "condition"` with the same frame-exact input as play, and `reload [files...]` (the scripts you edited go into the running game; every node keeps its values; a script that does not compile is left as it was). Every answer lists the errors the game printed since the last one, with their call chain. Loopback only, with a token; the project is not changed.

## Before an export

`godotwright export [path] [--preset name]` (godot_export): compares export_presets.cfg with what the scripts and scenes load. Godot leaves excluded files out even when something preloads them, and exports plain data files (text, binary, GeoJSON, cfg, XML, YAML) only when include_filter names them (JSON and imported CSV are resources); both work in the editor and break in the build. Also: paths built at run time under an excluded folder, and whether export templates are installed.

## Measuring performance

`godotwright perf [path] --scene res://x.tscn [--input "..."] [--budget 16.6]` (godot_perf): runs the scene headless and reports frame-time p50/p95/p99/max against a budget, the physics step apart, the slowest frames with what changed on them, node and orphan counts, and the change since the last run of the same scene.

## Seeing the game run

`godotwright check --scene res://x.tscn` (godot_check with scene or run_frames) runs a scene headless and returns what it printed: put print() calls in the code under test and read them back.
## Lessons from real projects

`godotwright lessons <words>` (godot_lessons) answers from 272 anonymous lessons learned in real Godot 4 projects (physics and moving decks, rendering and shaders, streaming large worlds, performance and frame-time measurement, 3D models, UI, audio, headless tests, patching shipped games): symptom, cause, fix and how to test. Pass a Godot message (`--error`, MCP `error`) to get the lessons that explain it; godot_check prints them under the errors too. `godotwright lessons add` (godot_lesson_add) keeps a lesson learned here, scrubbed of names, paths and code, on this machine only. `godotwright learn gaps` lists the Godot errors no rule or lesson explains yet.
`godotwright dream` (godot_dream) looks back between sessions (the learning file, the project's journal, and with `--transcripts` this project's Claude Code and Codex transcripts, kept only as anonymous facts) and proposes draft lessons for recurring Godot errors, "use X, not Y" project hints for guessed API names, lessons to merge, retire or rewrite, and verdicts to resolve, each with its evidence. Deterministic, local, nothing changes until `--apply`; `godotwright undo` takes an apply back. An apply also keeps a short "Godotwright lessons for agents" block in the project's AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md.
## Hooks for agents

`godotwright hook <event>` reads a Claude Code hook's JSON on stdin and prints hook JSON: `post-edit` reviews the Godot file just edited and returns its errors (blocking) or warnings (as context), `post-bash` adds the lessons that explain Godot errors in a command's output, `stop` names review errors still open in files changed this session (once), and `session-start` describes the Godot project. It prints nothing when it has nothing to add, never fails the agent, and `GODOTWRIGHT_HOOKS=0` turns it off. The Claude Code plugin wires all four.
## Porting Godot 3 scripts

`godotwright migrate` (MCP: godot_migrate) shows the mechanical Godot 3 to 4 rewrites it would make, `--write` applies them, and it lists what still needs a hand. Then `godotwright review`.
## Find usages

`godotwright usages <name>` (godot_usages): every place a function, signal, node, group, input action, autoload or res:// path is used, offline. Call it before renaming, moving or deleting.

## Unused files and what loads what

`godotwright deps unused|why <file>|of <file>|cycles [--path dir]` (godot_deps): follows what loads what from where the game starts (main scene, autoloads, every res:// path in project.godot, export include filters, the shipped file list in godotwright.json, add-ons, tests, editor scripts) through ext_resource, preload, load, class_name, folders and file names the code builds paths from, textures next to models and import settings. `unused` lists files nothing reaches, biggest first; `why` gives the chain from the game to a file; `of` lists what a scene loads with it and what it can load later; `cycles` finds scenes that load each other through ext_resource, which Godot cannot load (it says "[ext_resource] referenced non-existent resource" about a file that is there).

## Godot's own view of a script

`godotwright code diagnostics|hover|definition|completion <file> [--line n --column n] [--code file|-]` (godot_code): asks Godot 4.7's own GDScript language server, started headless as an editor and kept warm for 10 minutes: diagnostics at the project's warning levels, the inferred type or signature under the cursor, where a name is defined, what can follow. `--code` analyses text that is not saved yet.

## Shaders

`godotwright shader [path]` (godot_shader): reviews every shader against Godot 4.7's shader tables and compiles it with Godot headless (`Shader.get_rid()` runs the full shader compiler without a GPU), errors as file:line; `check` compiles every .gdshader headless too. `--gpu` (godot_shader `gpu: true`) adds the GPU pass. `godotwright shaders [path]` (and `check --shaders`, godot_check `shaders: true`) is that GPU pass: it draws every spatial, canvas_item, particles and sky shader on the Compatibility renderer (xvfb-run on Linux without a display), parses fog shaders, and reports errors at the line in the .gdshader, .gdshaderinc or .tres/.tscn, with the Godot 4 form of Godot 3 code; it adds what only the GPU driver rejects (a uniform block that is too big, a sampler array indexed by a variable).

## Visual tests

`godotwright screenshot --scene res://x.tscn --baseline [file-or-name]` (godot_screenshot `baseline`, "auto", a .png path or a name whose settings are kept in <name>.json): the first picture becomes a baseline in .godotwright/baselines/ (Godot does not import dot folders, so it can be committed); later pictures are compared pixel by pixel: unchanged as one line of text, or the percent changed, the box of the largest change, the mean shift, up to five areas of change (and how far one moved), where and a brightness shift, and a diff picture in red, as an error beyond `threshold`. Blank pictures are named. Scenarios take screenshots on chosen frames, and `godotwright ci` compares every named baseline. Renders are deterministic (fixed fps and fixed seeds).

## Undo

`godotwright undo [path] [--steps n] [--list] [--force]` (godot_undo): every Godotwright write (scene and project edits, renames with their file moves, migrations, fixes, model builds inside the project) keeps the files as they were in .godot/godotwright/journal/ (the last 40). Undo puts back the newest writes first; a file changed after the write stops the undo, so later edits are not lost unless `--force`.

## Rename and move

`godotwright rename <from> <to> [--write]` (godot_rename): renames a name or moves a res:// file everywhere at once, with a dry run first, and checks the review before and after.

## Project settings, input map, autoloads

`godotwright project set <key> <value>`, `project input add <action> --key Space --joy-button A`, `project autoload add <Name> <res://file>` (godot_project_edit with op set, unset, input_add, input_remove, autoload_add, autoload_remove): changes project.godot with checks, touching only that entry. Dry run first, `--write` (write: true) applies.

## Screenshots

`godotwright screenshot [path] --scene res://x.tscn` or `--model car.glb --view front,side,top,iso` (godot_screenshot, returns the PNG): renders with Godot's Compatibility renderer (software OpenGL works; xvfb-run on Linux without a display) and says how much of each view is drawn and where.

## Play input and watch values

`godotwright play [path] --scene res://x.tscn --input "10 tap jump; 20 hold right 30" --watch Player.position --watch Player.is_on_floor()` (godot_play): runs the scene headless, gives each input on exactly that physics frame, and returns the watched values per frame. Deterministic. Use it to see that the game does what the code says. `--until "Player.is_on_floor() == true"` stops at the first frame a condition holds, `--signal Player.landed` records when a signal fires with its arguments, `--summary` gives one line per watched value, and `--expect "Player.health > 0"` checks a claim (exit 1 when one fails). Runtime errors come with their GDScript call chain and a repeat count.

`godotwright ci [path]` and `godotwright scenario [path]`: `ci` runs the review, `check`, the tests (when GUT or GdUnit4 is installed) and the scenarios, and prints one markdown table, exit code 1 when a step fails. A scenario is a JSON file in `.godotwright/scenarios/`: `{"scene": "res://main.tscn", "input": "10 tap jump", "frames": 70, "expect": ["Hero.velocity.y == -400 @ 10", "Hero.is_on_floor() == true"]}`. An expectation is `<Node.property> <==|!=|>=|<=|>|<> <value> [@ frame]`, checked on the last frame when none is given; optional `until` (stop when it holds; fails when it never does) and `signals` (a claim on one, `Hero.landed >= 1`, counts how often it fired). Keep one when you finish a change: `godot_scenario` op `save` (or `godotwright scenario --save <name>`) takes the same arguments as godot_play, runs it once more and writes it only when every claim holds; op `run` runs them. `--junit <file>` on `ci`, `test` and `scenario` writes JUnit XML for GitLab, Jenkins or Azure test tabs.

## Unit tests

`godotwright test [path]` (godot_test): runs the project's GUT or GdUnit4 tests headless and returns the totals and only the failing tests with res://file:line and message. Needs Godot and GUT or GdUnit4 in res://addons.

## Scene edits

`godotwright scene add|remove|set|connect|disconnect|script <scene.tscn> ...` (godot_scene_edit with op add_node, remove_node, set, connect, disconnect, attach_script): changes a scene with checks against Godot 4.7 and the node's script, touching only those lines. Node paths are relative to the root ("."). Dry run first, `--write` (write: true) applies.

## Fix loop

`godotwright review --only-new` (godot_review with only_new: true): after the first review, only the findings that are new since the last one in full, the rest as one short line each, and how many are fixed.

## Workflow for 3D models

0. `godotwright model brief "<thing>"` (godot_model_brief): one page with the kind to start from, parts, size, rules and the order of work. Start here if you are a small model.
1. `godotwright model identify "<thing>"` (or the MCP tool godot_model_identify): what it is, its parts, typical size, pivots, what to anticipate.
2. `godotwright model build <kind> -o out.glb --set name=value --collision convex|trimesh|heightmap` (collision shapes on import; `heightmap` for terrain tiles writes `<name>.heightmap.tres` and a ready `<name>.tscn` with a StaticBody3D) from a ready-made kind (`godotwright model kinds`), or `--spec file.json` for your own tree of named parts (`godotwright model spec` explains the format).
3. `godotwright model view out.glb` (godot_model_view): front, side and top views as text, a table of the parts, and parts that do not touch the rest.
4. `godotwright model lint out.glb --archetype <thing>` (godot_model_lint): score and what-it-should-be checks. Fix every error.

Conventions: units are metres, +Y is up, the front of a model faces +Z, the model stands on y = 0, every moving part is its own node with its pivot at its origin.
Looks: built models carry seamless textures with normal maps for brick, roof tiles, slate, wood, bark, leaves, grass, stone, concrete, asphalt, plaster, sand and water (inside the .glb), and PBR presets for glass, tinted glass, chrome, steel, aluminium, brass, paint, plastic, canvas and glowing lights. In a spec, use `bevel` on boxes and cylinders for rounded edges, `lumps` on ellipsoids for organic shapes, the `tube` shape for frames, rails and pipes, and `"texture": "<pattern>"` on a custom material to draw a pattern in its own colour.
